rules.RESEARCHED_INITIAL: At least one directly relevant calibrated claim exists, including limitations or counterevidence; this is not approval or saturation.
rules.PARTIAL: Relevant claims cover only part of the capability or rely on indirect transfer.
rules.WEAK_GAP: Only adjacent evidence exists; dedicated research is required before curriculum use.

coverage.gap: Self-awareness needs a non-ruminative, non-surveillance operational definition and Egyptian-language testing.
Egyptian Arabic emotion vocabulary and low-literacy recognition testing remain absent.
Practice-by-practice dose, contraindication, and local acceptability are unresolved.
No direct everyday cognitive-flexibility intervention synthesis has been appraised.
Values clarification needs autonomy, family-duty, religion, and power-sensitive Egyptian testing.
Identity intervention evidence is sparse and role-transition evidence for diverse Egyptian adults is missing.
Dignity and self-respect remain distinct from self-esteem scores; Egyptian meanings and non-contingent wording need direct testing.
High risk of bias, cultural framing, adverse reactions, and behavior transfer require further work.
The anti-blame boundary is supported, but the exact Egyptian responsibility script requires structural, legal, linguistic, and user review.
Real-world Egyptian family, financial, work, and service decisions remain untested.
A standalone self-guided problem-solving protocol and escalation boundary are not validated.
Dose, context stability, relapse, disability, and structural feasibility need testing.
Behavior effects are small and Egyptian autonomy and constraint meanings need testing.
Flexible discipline needs a direct non-moralizing operational definition and counterevidence.
Ordinary attention supports outside digital contexts and across Egyptian work and care settings are under-researched.
Egyptian platform practices, affordability, essential device use, harassment, and work dependence need direct study.
Local shift work, caregiving, housing, climate, medical red flags, and practice dose need professional review.
Movement alternatives for disability, heat, safety, space, illness, and unpaid labor require local testing.
Stress literacy needs clear help thresholds and non-individualized structural framing.
Avoidance of adversity romanticization and Egyptian protective-factor validation remain required.
Safe training errors are now separated from loss and injustice, but adult Egyptian transfer, accountability, and trauma review remain pending.
Most evidence is clinical or laboratory-based and cannot define a self-guided dose.
Egyptian family, housing, finance, gender, workplace power, and retaliation scenarios need review.
Transfer from specialized programs to ordinary self-guided communication is limited.
Listening-specific outcomes, accessibility, and unsafe disclosure boundaries are under-researched.
Conflict de-escalation, power imbalance, and non-confrontation alternatives require dedicated evidence.
Repair must remain distinct from forgiveness, reconciliation, contact, and restored trust in local scenarios.
Trust formation and justified mistrust need direct evidence across family, services, work, and digital contexts.
Everyday Egyptian adult relationship structures and interdependence need qualitative work.
Evidence is mostly associational and student-weighted; Egyptian formation, maintenance, endings, reciprocity, and adult-life transitions need direct research.
Direct caregiving evidence is narrow and clinical; privacy, hierarchy, violence, family diversity, consent, and everyday communication need broader Egyptian study.
Violence-risk escalation and locally safe lower-arousal options need professional review.
Envy is covered mainly in social-media comparison research and needs broader relational and cultural evidence.
Offline comparison, useful benchmarking, class, status, gender, and family expectations need Egyptian evidence.
Intervention choice, direction of causality, solitude distinction, and Egyptian adult evidence remain limited.
Current verified Egyptian pathways and observed service use remain incomplete.
Causal training evidence and realistic Egyptian practice under care, transport, informal work, fatigue, and scarcity remain weak.
Current Egyptian inflation, debt, informal finance, consumer protection, and no-income alternatives require research.
Evidence is mainly classroom-based and needs adult and non-student transfer.
Egyptian sectors, informal employment, job insecurity, harassment, shifts, and organizational responsibility need study.
Avoiding one-grand-purpose pressure and testing plural values and roles in Egypt remain required.
Review quality is poor and burden, exclusion, safety, unpaid labor, and local opportunities need study.
Evidence comes from specialized science instruction; pluralistic Egyptian everyday ethics and behavior transfer remain untested.
Civic responsibility, rights, collective action, Egyptian safety, political neutrality, and structural limits require dedicated local review.
